name: Arcturus Defense Solutions SAR-3 'Warden'
description:
The SAR-3 Warden is Arcturus' purpose-built law enforcement rifle, designed for corporate police forces operating in dense urban environments. The weapon features an integrated IFF transponder that cross-references targets against Arcturus' citizen database in real-time, providing color-coded BCI overlays that identify corporate employees, registered civilians, known offenders, and unidentified individuals. The fire-control system includes an optional compliance lock that prevents firing on targets tagged as corporate assets.

Chambered in 5.56mm caseless with low-velocity frangible rounds as the default load, the Warden prioritizes minimal collateral damage in populated areas. The barrel is ported for reduced muzzle velocity, and the onboard computer tracks every round fired with GPS coordinates, timestamp, and target bearing for post-incident review. Every trigger pull generates a record.

The Warden is the most surveilled weapon in production. Its operators cannot fire without creating an audit trail, cannot target corporate-flagged individuals without override authorization, and cannot disable the tracking systems without triggering an alert. For corporate police this represents accountability. For everyone else, it represents a weapon that tells its manufacturer who you shoot, where, and when.
specifications:
caliber: 5.56mm caseless frangible
effective_range: 300m
rate_of_fire: 700 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 30 rounds
weight: 3.3 kg
tactical_use: The SAR-3 is optimized for urban policing operations where collateral damage and civilian casualties create liability. The IFF system prevents friendly-fire incidents against corporate personnel, and the audit trail ensures every engagement is documented. In practice, the compliance lock creates a dangerous delay when an operator needs to engage a target near a corporate-flagged individual — the system requires manual override confirmation that costs critical seconds.
cultural_context: The Warden embodies the surveillance state with a trigger. Corporate police carrying SAR-3s are sometimes called 'Wardens' themselves, and the weapon's data-collection capabilities have made it a symbol of corporate overreach. Activists argue that a weapon that identifies targets by social database is a weapon of social control. Arcturus argues it prevents exactly the kind of indiscriminate violence that gives weapons manufacturers a bad name.
story_hooks: The Warden's IFF database was updated with incorrect civilian tags — a protected witness was reclassified as a known offender, making them a valid target for every SAR-3 in the district.
A former corporate police officer has a decommissioned SAR-3 with its compliance lock removed. The audit trail still works — but now it records for whoever hacked the upload destination.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, angular assault rifle with a distinctly corporate aesthetic. The SAR-3 Warden presents itself as a tool of institutional authority—squared-off receiver, integrated upper rail system, and a prominent forward-mounted sensor array that gives it an almost insectoid appearance. The design prioritizes ergonomic precision over aggressive styling.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm | Barrel length: 41 cm | Receiver width: 6.5 cm | Height with rail mounts: 12 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and manageable at 3.3 kg—designed for extended urban patrols without fatigue. The weight distribution favors the grip, making it feel stable in close-quarters scenarios typical of dense metropolitan environments.
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade polymer composite chassis with reinforced aluminum alloy receiver sections. The barrel is hardened steel with port venting.
physical_description.finish: Matte anthracite polymer body with brushed aluminum rail sections. Surfaces show a subtle anti-reflective treatment to minimize tactical glint.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with anthracite accents. Arcturus corporate blue accent piping along the receiver and grip. Raised titanium-colored sensor modules.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with integrated palm swell. The controls feature haptic feedback zones—raised ridges indicate safety and fire-mode selectors. Rubberized trigger guard.
distinctive_features: Integrated IFF transponder module mounted above the receiver—spherical sensor with faint blue optical indicator
Forward-mounted target acquisition pod with multi-spectrum lens array
Digital readout display set into the left side of the upper receiver (small monochrome LCD showing round count, audit status, compliance lock indicator)
Ported barrel with enlarged venting ports visible from the side
Compliance override button—recessed and color-coded red—positioned at the lower receiver
GPS module antenna protruding slightly from the charging handle assembly
Serial plate stamped with 'AUDIT LOGGING ACTIVE' warning in Arcturus branding font
Ambidextrous safety lever with three detents: SAFE, FIRE, AUDIT-HOLD
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Large Arcturus Defense Solutions logo embossed on the left side of the receiver. Model designation 'SAR-3 WARDEN' stamped in corporate sans-serif font beneath the rail. Serial number and compliance certification visible on a polished aluminum name plate riveted to the lower receiver. Subtle repeated text reading 'EVERY ROUND LOGGED' etched into the grip.
physical_description.condition_typical: Corporate police weapons are meticulously maintained—expect pristine condition with no visible wear, though field units show minor surface scratches from duty gear contact. The sensor array is consistently clean and protected. No modifications permitted by operators; compliance violations trigger automatic deactivation and retrieval.
